_note: Aruba PoE budgets from the swarm lane's datasheet research. Where a chassis has modular PSUs the CONSERVATIVE single-PSU figure is recorded, because over-stating a budget lets impossible power configurations through - the exact failure this simulator exists to prevent. The published maximum is stated in each note.

poe.notes: JL256A: 370 W PoE+ from the fixed internal PSU. Optional X372 external supply raises it.
JL258A: 125 W PoE+ budget, fanless 8-port model running from an external adapter, no EPS option.
JL074A: chassis has 2 modular PSU slots (supplied separately). 370 W is one 680 W JL086A; one 1050 W JL087A gives 740 W and two give the published 1440 W max. Conservative single-PSU figure recorded.
JL679A: 139 W Class 4 PoE budget from the fixed PSU, fanless 12-port model.
JL677A: up to 370 W Class 4 PoE from the fixed power supply.
JL675A: 370 W Class 4 PoE. A separate 740 W SKU (R9Y04A) exists; this is the base model.
JL725A: up to 370 W Class 4 PoE from the fixed 500 W PSU.
JL727A: 370 W (fixed 500 W PSU) is the base SKU; JL728A is the 740 W variant with a 950 W PSU.
JL661A: 2 modular PSU slots. 370 W is one 680 W JL086A; one 1050 W gives 740 W and two give the published 1440 W max. Conservative single-PSU figure recorded.
R8N87A: 'PoE capability 370 W Class 4' confirmed against the vendor series page; the wattage in the name is the PoE budget, not the PSU rating (max power 455 W with PoE).
R8N85A: 370 W Class 4 PoE confirmed; the 740 W figure in the series blurb belongs to R9Y03A, not this model.

NO PUBLISHED POE BUDGET. The spec sheet lists only 'Power supply: internal 500 W' and 'max power consumption 500 W including PoE' - 500 W is the PSU rating, not an allocation to powered devices, and with 30 W internal draw at most ~470 W is deliverable. Unlike ES-24-250W and ES-48-500W, whose sheets explicitly state 'Total PoE available', this one has no such row. The earlier 500 W was a model-name guess and is withdrawn.
